title: Post-deploy Quiet Hour Rituals and Release Transcript
content:
Context:
This is a compact, pragmatic companion doc for medium-impact deployments (model flips, routing changes, infra-side config updates) that are targeting low-traffic windows. The goal: define a short, repeatable 'Quiet Hour' ritual (30–90m) and capture an operational transcript and release notes draft. This lives alongside the main rollout calendar and preflight checklists (see linked artifacts).

Why 'Quiet Hour'?
- Focused observation immediately after traffic changes reduces time-to-detect regressions.
- Keeps cognitive load low for on-call and launch crew: short checklist, tight telemetry targets, explicit escape hatches.
- Lightweight: suitable for fast followups and postmortems.

Summary of this deployment (placeholder values)
- Release tag: release/2026.11.22-quiethour
- Primary change: enable adaptive KV cache warming and routing heuristic v2 for hosted-api models
- Target populations: 2% global traffic, canary lane -> progressive ramp to 30% over 12h if green
- Owners: Aisha (release lead), Luca (runtime), Rina (telemetry), Tommy (rollout comms)

Preflight quick checks (30–60m before traffic shift)
- Code/Config:
  - PR merged: GH-PR-1347 (✓)
  - Short smoke deployed to staging and sanity tests passed (✓)
  - Feature flags staged and default-off in prod (✓)
- Telemetry & Alerts:
  - Baseline snapshots taken for: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost-per-request, error-rate, backend queue depth (timestamped)
  - Alert thresholds reviewed and temporarily suppressed where noisy (list suppression IDs in linked artifacts)
- Rollback & Contingency:
  - Rollback play: immediate feature-flag off + region abort route (ops-rollback-quick) documented
  - Hotpatch owner assigned and reachable during window: runtime-oncall + release lead
- Comms:
  - #release-watch channel created, pager duty rotation confirmed
  - Stakeholder ping list: eng-ops, product-hosted-api, eng-sre, support

Quiet Hour ritual (T0 = change applied) — recommended duration: 60m
- T0 (change flips to 2%): post message to #release-watch with timestamp and short summary
- T0+2m: smoke traffic run (ramped synthetic) — verify no 5xx spikes, end-to-end lat within 1.5x baseline
- T0+5m: sanity checks (manual):
  - sample 10 requests from canary lane and verify output shape and KV-cache warmup behavior
  - check logs for new error classes (use log query: "runtime.kv_warmup.error")
- T0+10m: telemetry check
  - check p50/p95 latency (telemetry-dashboard URL) — if p95 > baseline*1.5 -> investigate
  - check internal QPS routing split, token cost delta, and cache hit-rate trend
  - ensure no resource saturation: GPU memory, host CPU, disk IO
- T0+20m: deeper smoke
  - run low-latency and long-sequence synthetic tests to observe seq-length tail behavior
  - verify KV cache eviction rates & KV miss latency distribution
- T0+30m: human checkpoint
  - release lead asks 'green/amber/red' in #release-watch. If amber, hold ramp; if red, initiate rollback.
- T0+45m: observability pass
  - correlate any elevated error patterns with request attributes (model, region, tenant)
  - check logs for increased assertion/timeout patterns
- T0+60m: decision and log
  - If still green, schedule progressive ramp plan (to 10% over next 3h etc.) and record transcript snippet in this doc
  - If amber, pause rollout and keep canary at 2% until fix; consider patch window

Gating thresholds (example numeric gates — tailor per release)
- Immediate abort (RED): sustained 5xx increase > 0.25% absolute and > 3x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes OR p99 latency > baseline*3
- Pause and investigate (AMBER): p95 > baseline*1.5 for > 10m OR a 20% drop in embed/cache hit-rate OR error classes that touch auth/charge flows
- Proceed (GREEN): no gating violations for 60m and user-impact metrics stable

Escalation contacts & channel map
- First escalation: runtime-oncall (pager: +1-555-0123)
- Second escalation: eng-sre lead (Slack: @eng-sre-lead)
- Product contact: product-hosted-api (Slack: @pm-hapi)
- Support triage: support-rotation (email: support@redwood.ai)

Post Quiet Hour transcript (fill in after run)
- T0: 2026-11-22T02:00:00Z — flipped feature flag to canary lane (operator: Aisha)
- T0+2m: synthetic smoke run -> 0 new 5xx, baseline p95 +4% (Luca)
- T0+5m: log sniff -> two WARNs from kv_warmup about transient misses, tracked GH-PR-1351 (Rina)
- T0+20m: p95 stabilized, cache-hit rose from 28% -> 46% over first 15m
- T0+30m: human checkpoint: GREEN — proceed with ramp plan to 10% over 3h (Aisha)
- Notes: observed mild prober-timeouts in ap-southeast-1; investigation tied to noisy peering; contingency: route fallback to region B until networking fix

Progressive ramp appendix (example plan if Quiet Hour green)
- 2% -> 10% over 3h (incremental: 2% every 30m until 10%)
- 10% -> 30% over 12h (if 3h stable at 10%)
- Automated rollback trigger at each step if gating thresholds breached

Draft release notes (user-facing / internal)
- User-facing summary (short):
  - "We improved inference warmup and routing which reduces cold-start latency on long sequences for many hosted API customers."
- User-facing details (long):
  - "Updated KV cache warming heuristics and routing policy allow more requests to benefit from warmed state earlier in a session. Expected improvement: lower p95 latency on long-sequence calls and a modest reduction in token cost for repeated conversational sessions. No API changes."
- Internal notes / caveats:
  - "This is a controlled rollout with progressive ramp. We observed region-specific network noise in ap-southeast-1 during canary; any users in that region should be monitored for increases in tail latency. If necessary, roll back via feature-flag and open GH-PR-1351 for fix."

Postmortem & follow-ups (to capture within 72h)
- Owners create a 72h followup note: include final metrics at 1h, 6h, 24h and any incident timeline if triggered (owner: Aisha)
- Telemetry: Rina to publish a brief metric diff showing p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta by region and tenant type (due: +24h)
- Runtime: Luca to file optimization ticket for KV miss timeout tuning (GH-ISSUE-xxxx)
- Docs: product to add feature description to hosted-api changelog (done when GA)

Appendix: Quick commands and dashboard links (placeholders)
- Telemetry dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/dashboards/quiethour-canary
- Log query examples: query("runtime.kv_warmup.error | json | top 50")
- Synthetic runner command: ./scripts/run-canary-smoke --profile quiet-hour --samples 50

Unresolved questions / unblockers:
- Should the Quiet Hour also include an automated synthetic that exercises long-sequence beams for every model variant? Pros: faster detection; cons: extra synthetic load and cost.
- Need to confirm default rollback contact for org-level customers — escalate to customer-success for decision.

Related artifacts:
- CONFLUENCE-4582: release runbook (canonical)
- GH-PR-1347: runtime change (merged)
- GH-PR-1351: kv-warmup warn handling (follow-up)
- JIRA-RL-9821: rollout calendar and stakeholder pings

Notes to self and future readers (informal):
- Keep this doc lean. If we have recurring Quiet Hour runs, consider templating a small Slack bot to post T0 check prompts and auto-capture the transcript snippets.
- When in doubt: prefer conservative ramps for infra-root changes; be bold for purely UI/UX text-only changes.

-- end of draft --

Action items (now):
- [ ] Fill in real timestamps if running tonight (Aisha)
- [ ] Attach final telemetry snapshots to this doc (Rina)
- [ ] Push follow-up GH issues for observed WARNs (Luca)
